newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down 3.43 pct on new listings.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down 3.43 pct on new listings.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed sharply lower on Wednesday on news that 33 more companies had been chosen for B share listings and a reaffirmation of the ban on domestic investors buying B shares, brokers said.
The index shed 2.162 points or 3.43 percent to close at 60.861.
Brokers said sentiment had been hurt by the market expansion plans and the reaffirmation of a ban on domestic investors from buying B shares.

Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai, whose 80 million B shares were listed today, also attracted capital away from other shares, brokers said. Kaikai ended at $0.304, up 18.75 percent from its issue price of $0.256 on volume of 12.67 million shares, half the combined volume of 24.5 million shares on the Shanghai B share market.
"The news will reduce the amount of capital in the market," one broker said. "Overseas investors have little interest in B shares right now given all the uncertainties in the market."

"The index is likely to test the key 58-point support level in the short term," a second broker said. "Some institutions are expected to support the index around that level." Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 32 down, seven flat and three up.
Bicycle maker Phoenix was the biggest loser on concerns about its results, falling $0.014 or 7.95 percent to $0.162 on volume of 177,000 shares.
Real estate developer Lujiazui performed poorly on selling by institutions, falling $0.040 or 4.62 percent to $0.826 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
The Shanghai A share market ended down modestly in sluggish trading on cautious sentiment, brokers said.

The A index edged down 0.919 or 0.10 percent to 935.651 points, on volume of 195.1 million shares worth 1.8 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index fell 10.651 points or 0.44 percent to 2394.988 points.
Shanghai AJ lost the most on profit-taking, down 1.35 yuan or 5.023 percent to 25.50 yuan on volume of 340,700 shares.
Retailer Yinchuan Xinhua, which listed 22.95 million A shares on Wednesday, ended at 9.60 yuan, up 137.04 percent from its issue price of 4.05 yuan on volume of 17.9 million shares.
